program_name: Digital Enterprise Technology Engineering (Master's degree) — Italian official name: Laurea Magistrale in Ingegneria delle Tecnologie per l'Impresa Digitale (ITID-LM). NOTE: this is the SECOND-CYCLE (master's) programme at https://corsi.unibs.it/en/digital-enterprise-technology-engineering-md, which is a DIFFERENT degree from the same-named FIRST-CYCLE bachelor's programme at https://corsi.unibs.it/en/digital-enterprise-technology-engineering (bachelor: open access with TOLC-I test, taught in Italian).
teaching_language: conflicting_or_unverified — most likely ITALIAN, but not confirmed. See uncertainty_notes for the full reasoning. Evidence pointing to Italian: the programme's official name and all official documentation (study plan 'ITIDLM_Piano di studio ciclo 2024_25.pdf', presentation 'PresentazioneLMIngTecnologieImpresaDigitaleAprile2023.pdf', Regolamento Didattico) are Italian-language; even the English-URL page https://corsi.unibs.it/en/digital-enterprise-technology-engineering-md is indexed with the Italian title 'Ingegneria delle tecnologie per l'impresa digitale'; and the programme does NOT appear on the University of Brescia's 'Study programmes taught in English' listing (https://www.unibs.it/en/english-study-programmes), which lists Civil and Environmental Engineering, Communication Technologies and Multimedia and Analytics and Data Science for Economics and Management. english_delivery_scope: conflicting_or_unverified — the teaching language of THIS master's degree could not be established with confidence from directly verifiable official sources. programme_status: phasing_out_second_year_only — THIS PROGRAMME IS NOT ACCEPTING NEW FIRST-YEAR APPLICATIONS FOR 2026/27. The official course pages state that from academic year 2026/27 only the second year of the course will be active, meaning there is no first-year intake and no new enrolment for incoming students. Only already-enrolled students continuing into the second year can attend. All admission-related fields below (admission_type, academic_requirements, entry test, deadlines, required documents) therefore describe the historical/last-published framework and are NOT APPLICABLE FOR NEW FIRST-YEAR APPLICANTS in 2026/27.
pre_evaluation_required: Yes (historically, and generally for all UNIBS master's degrees) — for candidates with a foreign qualification, pre-evaluation/pre-assessment by the relevant Commission is compulsory for open-access master's degrees in the Economics, Engineering and Law areas, to verify curricular and personal-preparation requirements. Applications are submitted through the PICA online platform with a EUR 20 fee. For 2026/27 the non-EU pre-assessment round closed on 15 March 2026 (noon, Italian time), with outcomes emailed around mid-May 2026. NOT APPLICABLE FOR NEW FIRST-YEAR APPLICANTS to this master's in 2026/27, because no first-year intake exists. [uncertain] Whether this specific programme was ever included in the LMINT (English-taught master's) scholarship scheme could not be verified — the LMINT scheme (13 scholarships for 2026/27) is reserved for English-taught master's degrees, and this programme's inclusion is doubtful given the Italian-language evidence.
entry_test_name: None — there is no named admission test for this master's degree (no TOLC, no CISIA test, no SAT). The master's is 'without restricted access' (accesso libero); admission depends on verification of curricular requirements and personal preparation. IMPORTANT DISAMBIGUATION: the TOLC-I test that appears in search results for 'Digital Enterprise Technology Engineering' belongs to the BACHELOR'S degree of the same name (https://corsi.unibs.it/en/digital-enterprise-technology-engineering), NOT to this master's. NOT APPLICABLE FOR NEW FIRST-YEAR APPLICANTS in 2026/27.
admission_type: open access (accesso libero / 'course without restricted access'), subject to verification of curricular requirements and adequacy of personal preparation — NOT APPLICABLE FOR NEW APPLICANTS in 2026/27, since only the second year of the course is active from A.Y. 2026/27. (The same-named bachelor's degree instead uses TOLC-I; do not confuse the two.)
academic_requirements: [NOT APPLICABLE FOR NEW FIRST-YEAR APPLICANTS 2026/27 — recorded as the last published framework.] Enrolment in the Master's Degree course in Ingegneria delle Tecnologie per l'Impresa Digitale requires possession of an Italian three-year Bachelor's degree (laurea) or university diploma, or an equivalent foreign qualification recognised as suitable. As for all UNIBS engineering master's degrees, curricular requirements are defined in terms of the degree class held plus the skills and knowledge acquired in previous studies (expressed as minimum ECTS/CFU in specified scientific-disciplinary sectors, SSD) as established in the programme's Didactic Regulations (Regolamento Didattico), and the adequacy of the student's personal preparation is assessed according to the procedures defined in those same regulations. The programme is two years / 120 ECTS and has a single curriculum ('Curriculum generale'). [uncertain] The exact SSD codes, per-SSD minimum CFU thresholds and the list of automatically-qualifying bachelor's classes could not be extracted because the official pages and the Regolamento Didattico PDF could not be opened directly.
language_requirements: [NOT APPLICABLE FOR NEW FIRST-YEAR APPLICANTS 2026/27 — last published framework, and itself unverified for this specific degree.] The University of Brescia general rule is that all master's degrees in the Economics, Engineering and Law areas require English proficiency at least at level B1 CEFR; in place of an official certificate, programmes may accept candidates who completed their previous studies in English or who passed English examinations during their academic career (the CLA university language centre certificate is also accepted). [uncertain] If this master's is in fact Italian-taught (the most likely case), international applicants would additionally need Italian language proficiency — the same-named bachelor's degree page states an Italian requirement at B2 level, with teaching materials possibly in other languages and optional courses available in English. Whether an equivalent Italian-language requirement formally applies to this master's could not be verified directly, and no programme-specific language requirement statement could be retrieved.
application_deadline_eu: Not applicable for 2026/27 — no first-year intake for this programme. [uncertain] For UNIBS master's degrees generally, EU and EU-equivalent citizens holding a foreign qualification apply for pre-assessment in dedicated annual rounds (a previous round ran 30 June – 21 July at noon Italian time), and matriculation deadlines for master's degrees vary by programme, typically running from summer through December. The specific EU deadline that would have applied to this programme could not be verified.
application_deadline_non_eu: Not applicable for 2026/27 — no first-year intake for this programme. For reference only, the general UNIBS pre-assessment procedure for non-EU candidates holding foreign qualifications and aiming to enrol in Italian- or English-taught master's degrees in 2026/2027 was open until 15 March 2026 (noon, Italian time) through the PICA platform (EUR 20 fee), with results notified by email around mid-May 2026. This university-level pre-assessment deadline is SEPARATE from the Universitaly pre-enrolment and student-visa procedure handled by Italian diplomatic missions abroad.
required_documents: [NOT APPLICABLE FOR NEW FIRST-YEAR APPLICANTS 2026/27 — last published general framework.] For the PICA pre-assessment application for UNIBS master's degrees: bachelor's degree certificate (or certificate of expected graduation), full academic transcript listing examinations and ECTS, evidence of language proficiency, copy of passport/identity document, curriculum vitae, and payment of the EUR 20 pre-assessment fee. For final enrolment, holders of foreign qualifications must provide the standard Italian documentation — Declaration of Value (Dichiarazione di Valore) from the competent Italian diplomatic mission, or a CIMEA Statement of Comparability/Verification, with legalised and translated diploma and transcript; non-EU candidates residing abroad additionally complete Universitaly pre-enrolment for the study visa. [uncertain] No programme-specific document checklist could be retrieved.
entry_exam_or_test: [NOT APPLICABLE FOR NEW FIRST-YEAR APPLICANTS 2026/27.] No entrance examination and no standardised admission test for this master's degree. Admission is a documentary assessment by the Programme Council: verification of curricular requirements (minimum CFU in the SSDs set out in the Didactic Regulations) plus verification of the adequacy of personal preparation according to the procedures in those regulations. [uncertain] Whether an interview (colloquio) is used when personal preparation is not automatically satisfied could not be verified. Again, the TOLC-I entry test associated with the same-named BACHELOR'S degree does not apply to this master's.

uncertainty_notes:
1) DIRECT PAGE ACCESS FAILED — MANDATORY CAVEAT: neither https://corsi.unibs.it/en/digital-enterprise-technology-engineering-md nor its /enrolling sub-page could be retrieved directly. Automated fetching returned HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed for corsi.unibs.it and HTTP 403 Forbidden for www.unibs.it and en.unibs.it (including the official study-plan PDFs); opening the site in a browser produced a Cloudflare 'Human Verification' challenge with no readable content. Completing or bypassing that bot-detection challenge is not permitted, so ALL content in this record was compiled from search-engine indexed snippets and cached summaries of the official pages, NOT from directly verified live pages. Quotes in source_quotes are indexed renderings and may differ in exact wording or reflect an earlier crawl.

2) TEACHING LANGUAGE — THE CRITICAL UNRESOLVED POINT: teaching_language and english_delivery_scope are set to 'conflicting_or_unverified' as instructed, because no directly verifiable official statement about the master's language of instruction could be obtained. The weight of evidence points to ITALIAN: (a) the programme's official designation is the Italian 'Ingegneria delle Tecnologie per l'Impresa Digitale' and even the /en/ URL is indexed under that Italian title; (b) all official course documents found are Italian-language (ITIDLM_Piano di studio ciclo 2024_25.pdf, PresentazioneLMIngTecnologieImpresaDigitaleAprile2023.pdf, ITID Regolamento Didattico); (c) the programme presentation page exists at an Italian-only path (www.unibs.it/it/cds-ingegneria-tecnologie-impresa-digitale-lm); (d) the programme does not appear in the indexed content of the University of Brescia's 'Study programmes taught in English' page, which does list Civil and Environmental Engineering, Communication Technologies and Multimedia and Analytics and Data Science for Economics and Management. Against this, some AI-generated search summaries asserted 'the program is offered in English' — but no underlying official quotation supporting that claim could be located, and such summaries appear to conflate (i) the English-language version of the UNIBS website with the teaching language, and (ii) this master's with the same-named bachelor's. CONCLUSION: do not treat this programme as an English-taught degree without a direct check of the live official page or of the course-unit list (Insegnamenti) showing the language of each teaching unit.

3) BACHELOR VS MASTER CONFUSION — HANDLED EXPLICITLY: there are two distinct UNIBS degrees with the same English name. The BACHELOR'S degree (https://corsi.unibs.it/en/digital-enterprise-technology-engineering) is a first-cycle course with open access via the TOLC-I test, explicitly taught in Italian with a stated Italian requirement of B2 and only optional courses in English. THIS RECORD describes only the MASTER'S degree at the '-md' URL. Any TOLC-I reference, any Italian-B2 statement, and the 'studying' page at /digital-enterprise-technology-engineering/studying that appeared in search results belong to the bachelor's and were excluded from the master's fields, except where quoted in source_quotes with an explicit disambiguation note.

4) ENROLMENT STATUS FOR 2026/27 — EXPLICIT ANSWER: this master's degree is NOT accepting new first-year applications for 2026/27; official indexed content states that from A.Y. 2026/27 only the second year of the course is active. All admission fields are therefore marked as not applicable for new applicants. [uncertain] Whether the programme is being closed outright or replaced by a successor degree could not be determined; no official statement about a replacement was found.

5) DEGREE CLASS: LM-29 (Electronic Engineering) is reported by indexed content but was not directly confirmed on a live official page; treat as [uncertain].

6) OTHER UNVERIFIED FIELDS: exact SSD codes and minimum CFU thresholds; the programme-specific language requirement (English level and any Italian level); the exact document checklist; the specific EU application/enrolment deadline; whether a personal-preparation interview is used; whether the programme was ever eligible for LMINT English-taught-master's scholarships; current tuition amounts; and the exact campus building. All are flagged [uncertain] in their fields.

7) SOURCE POLICY: only unibs.it / corsi.unibs.it / www2.unibs.it URLs were used as evidence, as required. Third-party aggregators (educations.com, Mastersportal, expertise.unibs.it aggregations of third-party data) appeared in search results but were not used as evidence.
